short: EEG+EMG fusion (M05) and overt-audio DTW targets (M02) are standard; the unseen-sentence claim lacks a cohort WER (M12), and no EMG-only arm or EMG regression is reported.
position: The paper [@kim2025reconstructing] changes two components: it adds 10 face and neck EMG channels to 128-channel EEG (M05), and it trains whispered and imagined inputs on the overt recording of the same sentence through phoneme-weighted DTW (M02). Both are standard: EEG and sEMG fusion for silent-speech synthesis, with single-modality ablations, appeared in 2023 [@li2023hybrid] and is not among the paper's 53 references, and the training recipe is the EMG voicing recipe [@gaddy2021improved] that NeuroTalk had moved to imagined EEG [@lee2023towards]. The sentence-disjoint test (M12) follows field practice, but the evaluation is behind the best comparable work: the open-vocabulary claim rests on phoneme accuracy and DTW-aligned MFCC distances, with no cohort word or character error rate. The strongest confound is muscle: overt EEG is kept at 0.5–200 Hz with no regression of the simultaneously recorded EMG [@sato2024delineating], and there is no EMG-only arm, so what EEG adds to EMG is not measured.
